payload.task_text:
Our company is organizing a team-building cooking workshop next month and I need you to prepare the materials. We want to feature three Chinese dishes that are relatively easy to make (rated as easy, i.e. a low difficulty score, in the recipe database), and cover different categories so we get some variety. Please search through the available recipe database to find three suitable dishes that meet these criteria.

Note: write all document content in English (dish names, ingredients, cooking steps, tips, and the shopping list).

Once you have selected the three recipes, I need you to create three deliverables in the workspace.

First, create a Word document called Workshop_Handbook.docx. This should serve as a detailed step-by-step cooking guide for participants. Start with a title "Cooking Workshop Handbook" as a top-level heading. Then for each of the three dishes, include a second-level heading with the dish name, followed by a paragraph listing all the required ingredients with quantities, and then another paragraph (or multiple paragraphs) walking through the cooking steps in order. At the end of the document, add a section called "Tips and Notes" with any general cooking advice that would help beginners.

Second, create a PowerPoint presentation called Workshop_Slides.pptx for the instructor to use during the workshop. The first slide should be a title slide with "Team Cooking Workshop" as the title. Then for each dish, create two slides: one slide with the dish name as the title and the ingredient list as the content, and a second slide with the dish name followed by "Steps" as the title and the cooking steps as bullet points. Finally add a closing slide with "Enjoy Your Meal!" as the title.

Third, create a PDF file called Shopping_List.pdf in the workspace. This should be a consolidated shopping list that combines all ingredients from all three dishes, organized neatly so that someone from our procurement team can use it to go shopping. Group similar ingredients together if possible and include the total quantities needed. The document should have a clear title "Shopping List for Cooking Workshop" at the top.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must first query the exact `早餐`, `素菜`, and `主食` category listings in one native-parallel response, select one low-difficulty candidate ID from each category, and retrieve the three exact-ID recipe details in a second native-parallel response. Require three distinct IDs/categories and source-supported low difficulty, then freeze each recipe's English name, full translated ingredients with quantities, ordered translated steps, and beginner tips. The three independent deliverables can then be created in one wave.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): One coder sub-agent owns Workshop_Handbook.docx and writes the exact title, one complete section for each of the three frozen dishes, ordered ingredients/steps, and Tips and Notes. Read it back and return its path and three-dish coverage checks.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): One coder sub-agent owns Workshop_Slides.pptx and creates exactly the title slide, two slides for each of the three frozen dishes, and the Enjoy Your Meal closing slide. Read it back and return its path, presentation ID, eight-slide count, titles, and dish coverage.

   3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 2): One coder sub-agent owns Shopping_List.pdf and consolidates all ingredients from the same three frozen recipes in English with combined quantities and clear grouping. Read it back and return its path, title, ingredient coverage, and quantity controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent must cross-check the same three dishes and ingredients across all deliverables and finish without another wave.

nodes.text:
Create a Word document for a team-building cooking workshop. Save it at exactly:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace/Workshop_Handbook.docx

Use ONLY the mcp__word__* tools. Every time a tool asks for "filename", pass the full absolute path above. All content must be exactly as given below (English).

Build sequence:
1. mcp__word__create_document(filename=<path>, title="Cooking Workshop Handbook", author="Company Cooking Workshop")
2. mcp__word__add_heading(filename=<path>, text="Cooking Workshop Handbook", level=1)
3. mcp__word__add_paragraph: "Welcome to our team cooking workshop! In this handbook you will find step-by-step instructions for three classic Chinese home dishes chosen for today: Stir-fried Garlic Scapes with Minced Pork (a hearty meat dish), Tomato and Egg Stir-fry (the most iconic Chinese vegetable dish), and Seaweed Egg Drop Soup (a light, comforting soup). All three are beginner-friendly. Read through everything once before you start cooking."
4. For EACH of the three dishes below, in this order:
   a. mcp__word__add_heading(level=2) with the dish name exactly as given.
   b. One paragraph beginning with "Ingredients:" listing all the ingredients text exactly as given.
   c. One paragraph PER step (each paragraph is one of the step lines given below, including its "Step N:" prefix).
5. Finally: mcp__word__add_heading(level=2) text="Tips and Notes", then one add_paragraph per tip line given below. Do NOT add anything after the tips.

=== DISH 1 ===
Heading (level 2): Stir-fried Garlic Scapes with Minced Pork
Ingredients paragraph:
"Ingredients: thinly sliced pork belly - 4 slices (approx. 20 g); garlic scapes - 1 bunch (approx. 190 g); cooking oil - 10 ml; garlic - 2 cloves; light soy sauce - 15 ml; salt - 2 g."
Step paragraphs:
"Step 1: Cut the garlic scapes into 5 cm sections and set aside."
"Step 2: Cut the thinly sliced pork belly into strips about 5 mm wide and 5 cm long, and set aside."
"Step 3: Smash the garlic cloves and chop them finely; set aside."
"Step 4: Heat the wok, add the 10 ml of cooking oil, and wait about 10 seconds for the oil to warm up."
"Step 5: Add the chopped garlic and stir-fry over medium heat for 10 seconds until it becomes fragrant."
"Step 6: Add the pork belly and 5 ml of the light soy sauce; stir-fry over medium heat for 30 seconds until the meat is cooked and lightly colored."
"Step 7: Add the garlic scapes to the wok along with the remaining 10 ml of light soy sauce and stir-fry for 30 seconds."
"Step 8: Add about 20 ml of water and stir-fry over medium heat for 5 minutes until the garlic scapes are slightly softened."
"Step 9: Finally add the 2 g of salt, stir-fry over medium heat for another 30 seconds, then remove from the heat and serve."

=== DISH 2 ===
Heading (level 2): Tomato and Egg Stir-fry
Ingredients paragraph:
"Ingredients: tomato - 1 (approx. 180 g); eggs - 2; cooking oil - about 8 ml; salt - 2-3 g (about 1 g mixed into the eggs, the rest added at the end); sugar - 0-2 g (optional); chopped green onion - 0-10 g (optional)."
Step paragraphs:
"Step 1: Wash the tomato."
"Step 2: Optional: peel off the tomato's outer skin."
"Step 3: Remove the stem and cut the tomato into pieces no larger than 4 cm (tomato chunks)."
"Step 4: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add about 1 g of salt, and beat well (this is the egg mixture)."
"Step 5: Heat the wok and add the cooking oil."
"Step 6: Once the oil is hot, pour in the egg mixture. Stir-fry until the eggs set firm and turn slightly golden (half-cooked eggs)."
"Step 7: Turn off the heat. Remove the half-cooked eggs to a plate, then turn the heat back on."
"Step 8: Add the tomato chunks. Press and stir them with the spatula for about 20 seconds, or until the tomatoes soften and turn juicy."
"Step 9: Return the half-cooked eggs to the wok and stir-fry evenly."
"Step 10: Add the remaining salt, the sugar (optional, for a sweeter version), and the chopped green onion (optional), and stir-fry evenly."
"Step 11: Turn off the heat and serve."

=== DISH 3 ===
Heading (level 2): Seaweed Egg Drop Soup
Ingredients paragraph:
"Ingredients: dried seaweed (nori/laver) - 10 g; eggs - 2, beaten; water - 1.5 liters; salt - 2 g; cooking oil - 5 ml; chopped green onion - about 5 g; sesame oil - a few drops to finish; peeled shrimp or dried baby shrimp - optional, to taste."
Step paragraphs:
"Step 1: Soak the dried seaweed in clean water for 15 minutes, then lift it out and drain well."
"Step 2: Heat the pot, pour in 1.5 liters of water, 5 ml of cooking oil, and 2 g of salt. Once the water boils, add the seaweed."
"Step 3: After the seaweed has boiled for 3 minutes, slowly pour in the beaten egg in a thin stream; the soup will be ready in about 30 seconds."
"Step 4: Sprinkle in the chopped green onion and simmer on low heat for 20 seconds."
"Step 5: Turn off the heat. Before serving, add a few drops of sesame oil; adding a little dried baby shrimp at this point also tastes great."

=== Tips and Notes ===
Each as its own paragraph:
"• Read the whole recipe through before you start cooking, so you know every step."
"• Prepare everything in advance (mise en place): wash and cut your ingredients, and measure out seasonings into small bowls before turning on the stove."
"• Keep the heat at medium as a beginner. If the pan starts to smoke or the garlic browns too fast, lower the heat."
"• Cook eggs gently: add them when the oil is hot, stir lightly, and remove them as soon as they set - they keep cooking from residual heat."
"• Season gradually. Add salt and soy sauce a little at a time and taste before serving - it is easier to add than to fix."
"• For a silky egg-flower soup, pour the beaten egg into the boiling soup in a slow, thin stream while stirring gently."
"• Always soak dried seaweed before cooking - it expands significantly, so a small amount goes a long way."
"• Handle knives safely: keep a firm grip and curl your fingertips inward while cutting."
"• Food safety: wash hands, tools, and boards that touched raw meat with hot soapy water, and never serve cooked food on the plate that held raw meat."
"• Teamwork: assign roles - one person preps, one stirs, one seasons, and one plates. Cooking together is the fun part of the workshop!"
"• The quantities in this handbook are for one serving of each dish; scale them up proportionally for more participants."

Verification (required): after building, call mcp__word__get_document_outline on the file, and confirm with mcp__word__get_document_text that the document starts with "Cooking Workshop Handbook", contains all three level-2 dish headings and all steps, and ends with the Tips and Notes section.

Report back: confirmation the file was created at the exact path, the outline of headings found, and any issues.
Build Workshop_Handbook.docx

Create a PowerPoint presentation for a cooking-workshop instructor. Save it at exactly:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace/Workshop_Slides.pptx

Use ONLY the mcp__pptx__* tools. Build exactly 8 slides with the content given below (all English).

Procedure:
1. Call mcp__pptx__create_presentation and note the returned presentation id. Pass that presentation_id explicitly in every later call.
2. Slide 1 (title slide): mcp__pptx__add_slide with layout_index=0 and title="Team Cooking Workshop". If the presentation created in step 1 already contains a leading blank/layout slide you didn't create, use mcp__pptx__get_presentation_info and mcp__pptx__extract_presentation_text after building to make sure there are no extra empty slides; if an undesired empty slide exists at any position, rebuild cleanly or work around it so that the final deck contains exactly the 8 slides described here, in this order.
3. Slides 2-7 (content slides): use add_slide with layout_index=1 and the title parameter set as specified. Then fill the content placeholder (usually placeholder index 1) using mcp__pptx__populate_placeholder with one string where each ingredient/step is on its own line joined by newlines. If populate_placeholder fails because there is no placeholder, use mcp__pptx__add_bullet_points(slide_index, placeholder_idx, bullet_points list) instead; if neither works for a slide, fall back to mcp__pptx__manage_text(operation="add") with a text box (left=1, top=1.8, width=8, height=5) containing the lines.
4. Slide 8 (closing): add_slide with layout_index=0 and title="Enjoy Your Meal!".
5. Save with mcp__pptx__save_presentation to the exact path above.

Exact slide content:

SLIDE 1 (title): "Team Cooking Workshop"

SLIDE 2 - title: "Stir-fried Garlic Scapes with Minced Pork"

"Add the chopped garlic and stir-fry over medium heat for 10 seconds until fragrant."
"Add the pork belly and 5 ml of the light soy sauce; stir-fry over medium heat for 30 seconds until the meat is cooked and lightly colored."
"Add the garlic scapes and the remaining 10 ml of light soy sauce and stir-fry for 30 seconds."
"Add about 20 ml of water and stir-fry over medium heat for 5 minutes until the garlic scapes are slightly softened."
"Add the 2 g of salt, stir-fry 30 seconds more, then serve."

SLIDE 4 - title: "Tomato and Egg Stir-fry"
Content lines:
"tomato - 1 (approx. 180 g)"
"eggs - 2"
"cooking oil - about 8 ml"
"salt - 2-3 g (about 1 g in the egg mixture, the rest at the end)"
"sugar - 0-2 g (optional)"
"chopped green onion - 0-10 g (optional)"

SLIDE 5 - title: "Tomato and Egg Stir-fry Steps"
Bullet points:
"Wash the tomato."
"Optional: peel off the tomato's outer skin."
"Remove the stem and cut the tomato into pieces no larger than 4 cm."
"Crack the eggs into a bowl, add about 1 g of salt, and beat well."
"Heat the wok and add the cooking oil."
"Once the oil is hot, pour in the egg mixture; stir-fry until the eggs set firm and turn slightly golden."

"Add the tomato chunks and press/stir with the spatula for about 20 seconds until soft and juicy."
"Return the eggs to the wok and stir-fry evenly."
"Add the remaining salt, the sugar (optional), and the chopped green onion (optional); mix evenly."
"Turn off the heat and serve."

SLIDE 6 - title: "Seaweed Egg Drop Soup"
Content lines:
"dried seaweed (nori/laver) - 10 g"
"eggs - 2, beaten"

"salt - 2 g"
"cooking oil - 5 ml"
"chopped green onion - about 5 g"
"sesame oil - a few drops to finish"

SLIDE 7 - title: "Seaweed Egg Drop Soup Steps"
Bullet points:
"Soak the dried seaweed in clean water for 15 minutes, then drain well."
"Bring 1.5 liters of water to a boil with 5 ml of oil and 2 g of salt; add the seaweed."
"After the seaweed boils for 3 minutes, slowly pour in the beaten egg; ready in about 30 seconds."
"Sprinkle in the chopped green onion and simmer on low heat for 20 seconds."
"Turn off the heat; add a few drops of sesame oil (and optional dried baby shrimp) before serving."

SLIDE 8 (closing): title "Enjoy Your Meal!"

Verification (required): after saving, call mcp__pptx__open_presentation on the saved file path and then mcp__pptx__extract_presentation_text to verify the saved file contains all 8 slides with the correct titles and content. Confirm the file exists at the exact path.

Report back: confirmation of creation, slide count, list of slide titles found in the saved file, and any issues.

Create a PDF shopping list for a cooking-workshop procurement team. Save it at exactly:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace/Shopping_List.pdf

Approach (use Python): use mcp__local__python_execute. First try `import reportlab`; if unavailable try `import fpdf`; use whichever works. If neither is importable, fall back to this chain instead: build the same content as a Word document with mcp__word__* tools (title as heading level 1, section names as headings level 2, items as paragraphs) at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-workshop-materials/workspace/_tmp_shopping.docx, then convert it with mcp__word__convert_to_pdf to the exact Shopping_List.pdf path above.

If using Python, generate a clean, readable PDF (use the built-in ASCII fonts such as Helvetica/Times - all content is plain English). Layout requirements:
- At the very top, title exactly: "Shopping List for Cooking Workshop"
- Below it, a short italic/normal intro line.
- Then 4 section headings and their grouped items, followed by a Notes section at the end. Bullet points for each item.

EXACT CONTENT:

Title: Shopping List for Cooking Workshop

Intro line: "Consolidated ingredient list for the three workshop dishes - Stir-fried Garlic Scapes with Minced Pork, Tomato and Egg Stir-fry, and Seaweed Egg Drop Soup. Quantities are for one serving of each dish; scale up according to the number of participants."

Section: Proteins and Eggs
- Eggs: 4 total (2 for Tomato and Egg Stir-fry, 2 for Seaweed Egg Drop Soup)
- Thinly sliced pork belly: about 20 g / 4 slices (for Stir-fried Garlic Scapes with Minced Pork)
- Peeled shrimp or dried baby shrimp: small amount (optional, for Seaweed Egg Drop Soup)

Section: Vegetables
- Garlic scapes: 1 bunch, about 190 g (for Stir-fried Garlic Scapes with Minced Pork)
- Tomato: 1, about 180 g (for Tomato and Egg Stir-fry)
- Garlic cloves: 2 (for Stir-fried Garlic Scapes with Minced Pork)
- Green onions: a small bunch, at least 10-15 g chopped in total (about 5 g for soup garnish, the rest optional for the stir-fry)

Section: Seaweed and Dry Goods
- Dried seaweed (nori/laver): 10 g (for Seaweed Egg Drop Soup)

Section: Pantry and Seasonings
- Cooking oil: 1 bottle (about 23 ml used in total: 10 ml + 8 ml + 5 ml)
- Light soy sauce: 1 bottle (15 ml used)
- Salt: 1 packet (about 5 g used in total: 2 g + 2-3 g + 2 g)
- Sugar: small amount, 0-2 g (optional, for the tomato stir-fry)
- Sesame oil: 1 small bottle (a few drops, to finish the soup)

Section: Notes
- Quantities are per one serving of each dish; if N participants share each dish, multiply accordingly.
- Check the venue kitchen pantry first - oil, salt, and sugar may already be available.
- Buy slightly more than listed to have buffer for the workshop.
- Water (about 1.5 liters for the soup) comes from the tap; no need to buy it.

Verification (required): after generating, call mcp__pdf-tools__get_pdf_info on the PDF path and mcp__pdf-tools__read_pdf_pages on page 1 to confirm the title "Shopping List for Cooking Workshop", all five section headings, and the item lines are present and readable. Also confirm with mcp__filesystem__get_file_info that the file exists in the workspace and note its size. If any verification shows missing text, regenerate and re-verify.

Report back: confirmation the file exists at the exact path, page count, and which sections were verified in the PDF text.
Build Shopping_List.pdf
